nodes.name: NF surface cleaning
nodes.procedure: NF with a size of 2.0 cm×3.0 cm was prepared. Sequentially, the NF was successively immersed in three different solutions for ultrasonic surface deoxidation: solution A, prepared by mixing 10 mL concentrated HCl with 30 mL ultrapure water; solution B, composed of 30 mL ultrapure water; solution C, consisting of 30 mL ethanol. Following the treatment, the NF was dried in an oven.

nodes.name: NiFe LDH/NF hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 10 mmol urea, and 4 mmol NH4F were sequentially weighed and dissolved in 40 mL of deionized water to generate solution D. Solution D was then poured into a Teflon-lined autoclave, and the dried NF was immersed in it. Then heated the mixture at 120°C for 6 h. After a while, the NF was taken out, underwent several washes, and then dried at 60°C. The final product obtained was NiFe LDH/NF.

nodes.name: RuO2/NF electrode fabrication
nodes.procedure: An ethanol solution (with a 50/50 vol split of water and ethanol) and an extra 30 μL of Nafion binder were employed to disperse RuO2 powder for the ink (5 mg mL-1). The resulting ink in a small centrifuge tube underwent approximately 30 min of sonication, followed by the pipette transfer of 240 μL of the ink dropwise onto a cleaned NF. The electrode was then fabricated after drying.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF shows characteristic NiFe LDH peaks with (003) peak shifted to 11.7° giving layer spacing of 8.0 Å, larger than 7.7 Å of NiFe LDH/NF, confirming successful C₂O₄²⁻ intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1b, distinctive XRD patterns are observed for both LDH electrodes... The layer spacing of NiFe - C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF (8.0Å)... is larger than that of NiFe LDH/NF (7.7Å), confirming the successful C₂O₄²⁻ intercalation into the NiFe LDH.

properties.description: Layered double hydroxide structure with green and blue layers

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectrum of NiFe-C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF shows characteristic C₂O₄²⁻ peak at 905 cm⁻¹, absent in pristine NiFe LDH/NF, confirming successful introduction of C₂O₄²⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectral displays that the characteristic peak of C₂O₄²⁻ at wave number 905 cm⁻¹ belongs to NiFe-C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF... while the pristine NiFe LDH/NF does not, which implies the successful introduction of C₂O₄²⁻ into pristine NiFe LDH/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF retains nanosheet structure of NiFe LDH/NF covering NF surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the SEM images... NiFe - C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF (Fig. 1d) retains the nanosheet structure of NiFe LDH/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping confirms presence of Ni, Fe, O, and C elements in NiFe-C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF nanosheets with C proportion of 2.40 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping images obtained from these nanosheets (Fig. 1e) via EDX analysis confirm the presence of Ni, Fe, O, and C elements, with the proportion of C being 2.40 wt%.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanosheet feature of NiFe-C₂O₄²⁻ LDH; HRTEM shows lattice spacing of ≈0.21 nm corresponding to (018) plane of NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images of NiFe - C₂O₄²⁻ LDH further confirm its nanosheet feature (Fig. 1f). The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Fig. 1g) reveals its lattice spacing of ≈ 0.21 nm, close to the theoretical interplanar spacing of the (018) lattice plane of NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms successful C₂O₄²⁻ intercalation: survey shows Ni, Fe, O, C; Ni 2p at 855.8/873.5 eV (Ni²⁺); Fe 2p at 711.5/724.5 eV (Fe³⁺), 707.4/719.5 eV (Fe²⁺); C 1s at 288.3 eV (C₂O₄²⁻); O 1s at 531.3 eV (C₂O₄²⁻).
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the outcomes of XRD, XPS, and Raman spectroscopy, the C₂O₄²⁻ is inserted into NiFe LDH/NF successfully.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at varying scan rates gives C_dl more than twice that of NiFe LDH/NF, indicating increased active surface area after C₂O₄²⁻ intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We found an increase in the C_dl of NiFe LDH/NF with the intercalation of C₂O₄²⁻, the value of NiFe - C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF is more than twice of NiFe LDH/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows lower charge transfer resistance R_ct ∼7.18 Ω for NiFe-C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF vs ∼9.81 Ω for NiFe LDH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 3d, the superior performance of NiFe - C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF (R_ct∼7.18Ω) compared to NiFe LDH/NF (∼9.81Ω, Table S1) is reflected in its lower charge transfer resistance.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows lower leaching after 24h at 1000 mA cm⁻²: NiFe-C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF has 0.049 mg L⁻¹ Ni and 0.066 mg L⁻¹ Fe vs 0.092 mg L⁻¹ Ni and 0.295 mg L⁻¹ Fe for NiFe LDH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After 24-hour chronoamperometry testing at 1000 mA cm⁻² we employed ICP-MS to quantify the leaching... leaching amounts of Ni are 0.049 and 0.092 mg L⁻¹ for NiFe - C₂O₄²⁻ LDH/NF and NiFe LDH/NF, respectively, while the corresponding leaching amounts of Fe are 0.066 and 0.295 mg L⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability test XPS Cl 2p shows absence of Cl species on NiFe-C₂O₄²⁻ LDH surface (vs present on NiFe LDH), confirming C₂O₄²⁻ repulsive effect against Cl⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. S13, the Cl 2p fine spectrum analysis of NiFe - C₂O₄²⁻ LDH after stability testing demonstrates the absence of Cl species on its surface. In contrast... NiFe LDH exhibits the presence of Cl species on its surface.
